title: The skeleton
examples: How many bones do we have?

explain.say: The human skeleton has about two hundred six bones in total.

items: The adult human skeleton has 206 bones.
This number is the total count.
It provides structure to the body.

explain.say: Now let me show you the real thing in 3D: the human skeleton. Look at the skull, the ribcage and the backbone. Tap any part, and I will tell you what it does.
Bones give our body important support so we can stand up straight.
The bones protect our soft and delicate internal organs inside.
Movement happens when bones connect at special places called joints.
Think about bending your arm at the elbow joint to wave hello.
When you walk, your leg bones move smoothly at the knee joint.

faq.q: Why is the skull so important for protection?
faq.a: The skull is a bony structure that completely encloses and protects the delicate brain inside. It is very strong to keep the brain safe from bumps.
asks: Does the skull protect the brain?

faq.q: What is the difference between support and protection?
faq.a: Support means holding you up so you can stand tall, while protection means keeping things inside safe from harm. Bones do both jobs.
asks: Can bones only do one job?

faq.a: A joint is the place where two or more bones meet together. These meeting points allow parts of your body to move.

faq.q: Do all joints allow the same type of movement?
faq.a: No, joints are different. Some only bend one way, while others let you move in many directions.
asks: Can I move my wrist like my shoulder?

faq.q: How many bones do babies have compared to adults?
faq.a: Babies actually have more bones when they are born than adults. Some bones join together as you grow bigger.

facts: The skeleton is made up of many different types of bones.
The rib cage protects the heart and lungs.
Joints allow bones to move relative to each other.

quiz.say: Which body part is primarily responsible for protecting the brain?
quiz.why: The skull is a hard, bony case that surrounds and protects the brain.

wrong.1: The rib cage protects the chest organs, not the brain.
wrong.2: The spine supports the back, but it does not surround the brain.
wrong.3: Joints are places of movement, not protective casings for the brain.

quiz.say: What is the main function of joints?
quiz.why: Joints are the connection points that allow bones to bend and move.

wrong.1: Support is the job of the bones themselves, not the joints.
wrong.2: Protection is done by the hard outer parts like the skull.
wrong.3: Structure is the overall shape, while joints allow parts to change shape.

quiz.say: If you bend your elbow, what part is allowing that action?
quiz.why: The elbow joint is the specific place where the bones meet to allow bending.

wrong.0: Muscles pull the bones, but the joint is the physical connection point.
wrong.1: The skeleton is the whole system; the joint is just one part of it.
wrong.3: The bone is the rigid part; the joint is the space between the bones.
